items.title: Alphonse Picou Interview, 1960-11-03
items.q: Oh, the trombone was called Bill Harrison.

ctx.x: Oh, the trombone was called Bill Harrison. Oh, Bill Harrison. Big Bill Harrison. Bill Harrison. I don't remember much about him. Where did he, was he over on this side of the river or come from the other side? On this side, yeah. This side? Yeah. Is he uptown or downtown here? Uptown. Uptown. Yeah. Did they have a bass, or a glennie, did they have a drummer? Huh? Did they have a drummer? A drummer? Uptown. With us. Oh yeah. At the paddock. Happy. Yeah, happy Goldston then. Yeah, happy golden, that's it. There was…

Well, you showed me your clarinet one time. It's 15 keys on it with a curved up bell. I noticed some of those keys don't even work anymore. You don't use all the keys? No. You work mainly with the holes in the clarinet? Yeah. Yeah, I noticed when you play high society, you don't use the keys very much. No.
